# /crav1-verify-build-against-spec

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Verify and fix](../../from-verify.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-verify-build-against-spec/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Map every v0 acceptance line to tests or UI checks and report pass, fail, or missing.

1.180.0: the tick offer for a task recorded merged sits inside Run next, label above `verify_rows.py tick --file <spec-folder>/verify.md --task <T#> --merged yes`, never after the ending; the tick is written only after a yes. A Not implemented row is verified first.

1.176.0: new status **Implemented, verified on branch** for evidence that passed on an unmerged work branch; a check that can only pass after the merge is pending. It becomes tick pending once the merge is recorded. `verify_rows.py set` keeps CRLF files CRLF and re-sorts a count line only when its ids change.

1.172.0: a rerun verifies again only the rows whose branch or tip moved since the last verify, or every row when spec.md, plan.md or tasks.md changed (`scripts/verify_rows.py scope`), and the reply says which rows were kept (`Kept from the last verify: T1, T3 (branch and tip unchanged).`). `verify_rows.py set --task T# --status <status> --evidence <evidence> --branch <b> --tip <sha> --yes` writes one row, recounts the TL;DR and records the tip under `## Row tips`.

1.171.0: with no hand-written steps, the reply's branch blocks come from the ready check (`walk_ending.ready_branch_blocks`), with descriptions, open tasks and the whole-branch entry; a task that waits on a merge is not offered.

1.170.0: a `T6 failed:` change line in the reply keeps the Verify cell's opening sentence and the sentence naming the cause, not the run detail; the ready check's Catch up first line uses the same short reason.

1.169.0: `verify.md` has no `Next:` line any more; the chat reply's Run next names the next step. The ready check still reads an older file that has one, and a Verified or Failed row there is never behind.

1.168.0: the chat reply is brief and built by `scripts/walk_ending.py --verify <state file>` (a wrapper for the shared ending script): `Verify — <slug>`, a `Result:` line with the counts, one line per task whose state changed since the last verify (`T6 failed: ...`, `T44 row dropped: not in tasks.md`), `Run next:`, Waiting for what you cannot act on now, then `Report: docs/specs/<slug>/verify.md`. Run next opens with a `**Catch up first**` block when something can be settled now: a plan note ([`/crav1-tighten-plan`](crav1-tighten-plan.md) <slug>`) and an uncommitted `verify.md` ([`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md), then `git push`). Then the next step: the reason once, the label on its own line and the command alone in its code span; there is no `Next:` line. The TL;DR, tables and branch detail stay in `verify.md`; the word `full` shows the TL;DR and Tasks overview in chat. The run reads only spec, plan, tasks, the previous `verify.md` and the reference a step names, not `build-map.md`, `claims.md`, `walk-progress.md` or a log. The live checks and `verify.md` are unchanged.

1.167.0: the Tasks overview has one row per T# in `tasks.md`; a row for a T# that `tasks.md` does not have is dropped and the reply names it. The ready check's Catch up first block names only this command for a behind task and a stray row.

1.149.0: the branch line, sub-branches, promotion, tick pending, a host-setup task, and the one next line are references files, each read only when that case applies. The rules are unchanged.

1.142.0: when [`/crav1-build-walk`](crav1-build-walk.md) opened this skill, do not print the case Next. The walk prints its one Next.

TL;DR of implemented vs not, then acceptance details in `verify.md`.

Before the tests, a local dependency preflight checks Azurite, database containers, and emulators the repo's tests name, and asks start, skip, or stop for one that is not running. A test skipped for a missing dependency blocks verified unless you chose skip; then `verify.md` lists it under Skipped tests. A missing dependency is a `BLOCKER:` line at the top of the summary, also in a headless run, which uses the two-pass questions file.

1.64.0: the TL;DR adds a Branches line (merged into the base, deleted-but-merged, rewritten, shared); demoable needs every work branch merged. Report only.

1.68.0: the `Sub-branches:` and `left behind:` lines, done when the top-level branches reached the base, and `merged, reverted on <base> (<sha>)`, report only.

1.69.0: the `Promotion:` line in the TL;DR and verify.md, with the optional `pipeline-runs` check; done stays merged.

1.136.0: the spec folder is `scripts/resolve_spec.py` (exact folder, then hyphen and space forms, then one unique playbook basename, spec title, or work-item name). Several matches are listed and the run stops. It does not pick the most recently edited tree. A task whose evidence passed, whose row is still `[ ]`, and whose pull request is recorded merged is **Implemented, verified, tick pending**. That is not Not implemented. Next skips tasks the ready check counts as done and names the first task that can start, one line per ready branch. The open checkbox stays a Gap. After a yes, the report may tick that one row. It does not re-implement.

1.137.0: `scripts/resolve_spec.py` also accepts one unique ordered token subsequence of a folder name, playbook basename, spec title, or work-item name (`cc 1.0` matches `cc-process-1-0`). Several matches are listed and the run stops. No match lists the nearest slugs.

1.144.0: the spec folder command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`. On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`. Elsewhere it is `python3`. The rule is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline-runs` | check the latest successful Azure DevOps runs behind the Promotion line (read-only) |
| Long reply? | `full` | show the TL;DR and Tasks overview in chat (1.168.0); the brief reply is the default |

## Runs when

Want proof against acceptance. Called by the user and by `crav1-build-task-agent`.

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 3 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: Spec, tasks, plan, and the running tree.

Reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, the previous `verify.md`, and the running tree. It does not open `build-map.md`, `claims.md`, `walk-progress.md` or a log unless a step names it (1.168.0).

## Writes

In short: `verify.md`, and one `[x]` on a tick-pending row after a yes.

Writes `verify.md`. After a yes on a tick-pending line, ticks that one `[ ]` row in `tasks.md`.

## Does not

Leaves `spec.md` and product code alone. Does not tick a row without a yes, and does not re-implement.

Limits and exceptions: does not run [`/crav1-fix-bug`](crav1-fix-bug.md) or [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md).

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-fix-build-gaps`](crav1-fix-build-gaps.md); [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md)
- Runs by itself: Calls no skill.
